neighbors.establishing_passage: The study evaluated ischemic-core overestimation and related it to baseline core volume, reperfusion, final infarct volume, and functional outcome in a 721-patient cohort.
The work showed that biomedical image-analysis challenge rankings can change with the sampled test cases and analysis choices.

ISLES'24 provides acute CT, follow-up MRI labels, and clinical variables for final-infarct prediction; the challenge paper describes predictive use rather than contribution-defined clinical profiling.

neighbors.identifier: Anatomical-phenotypic graph learning for interpretable acute ischemic stroke prognosis prediction from non-contrast CT and clinical data, Biomedical Signal Processing and Control, 2026
neighbors.establishing_passage: The search summary reports prognosis prediction on ISLES 2024 using NCCT and clinical data; subgroup and contribution-census details could not be inspected.
In 3,555 CTP scans, reduced temporal sampling yielded ICC 0.97–0.99 for core and hypoperfusion volumes and changed some treatment decisions.
The study varied temporal resolution in stroke CTP and assessed quantitative perfusion parameters, lesion contrast, map quality, and diagnostic accuracy.
The study simulated temporal subsampling and noise and assessed reproducibility of parametric maps and core volumes.
Simulation showed that Tmax reflects delay, dispersion and MTT and is sensitive to experimental timing; temporal interpolation was recommended.
A digital perfusion phantom was used to calibrate software-specific CTP lesion thresholds across deconvolution methods.
Commercial CTP packages produced substantially different estimates of ischemic core and penumbra volume.
User-selected image-intensity discretization settings materially affected radiomic feature values and reproducibility.
